title: Screen Light Reflecting in Your Glasses? Adjust the Selfie Angle
description: If screen light reflects in your glasses, slightly change the phone and face angle, reduce brightness and check a saved selfie.
direct: Tilt the phone slightly or turn your face until the screen reflection moves away from your eyes. Take a test photo before changing the lighting again.
figureAlt: An adult changes phone angle to investigate screen reflections in glasses.

cards.choice.heading: Find the reflection path
cards.choice.body: Look for a bright screen-shaped patch over the eyes. A small movement may shift it, but a different lens coating, screen position or ambient lamp can change the result. Do not expect one universal angle to remove every reflection.
sections.explain.heading: Use the room light too
sections.explain.body: Soft light from a nearby window or lamp can reduce dependence on a bright screen. Check whether another light is producing the glare before changing the phone repeatedly. Avoid uncomfortable brightness. This is a lighting adjustment, not a digital glare-removal or eyeglass-retouching feature.
sections.practice.heading: What GlowPop offers
sections.practice.body: Our iPhone app provides a front-camera mirror with adjustable screen color and brightness while the camera stays open. The first five photos are free, including white-light photos; Pro unlocks unlimited photos and video recording. Reflections depend on the scene and glasses, so this guide promises no measured improvement. Keep your favorite saved test as a reference for the next selfie.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: What if tilting the phone also changes the framing too much?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: Keep the viewpoint that works for your face and turn slightly instead. You can also lower screen brightness and use soft room light.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: Should I remove my glasses to solve the glare?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Keep them on if they are part of how you want to look. Check a saved photo at normal size and adjust only if the reflection hides what matters.

steps.step-1.text: Open GlowPop: Selfie Glow Camera with a neutral screen color and moderate brightness. Keep the whole face in frame.
steps.step-2.text: Move the phone slightly above or to one side and turn your face a little. Watch the eyes, framing and facial shadows together.
steps.step-3.text: Take a photo and inspect the saved result. Try a small brightness or angle change if a screen reflection still covers the eyes.
